key_insight: The paper argues that full-duplex agents should not be judged only by whether they keep talking or stop talking. It introduces in-turn adaptation: the ability to keep speaking while correctly incorporating a listener’s contribution, such as a correction, missing word, or clarification.
problem_solved: Current full-duplex evaluation is too binary to capture realistic overlapping speech behavior. It misses whether an agent can distinguish different listener intents and adapt its ongoing utterance accordingly.
method: Introduces Duplex Cue, an evaluation framework for in-turn adaptation in full-duplex voice agents.
Separates listener intent into categories such as backchannel, collaboration, and interruption.
Evaluates whether the speaker behavior adapts appropriately during overlapping speech, rather than only measuring continue-vs-yield decisions.
impact: This gives researchers and practitioners a more realistic way to measure conversational agents in live, overlapping dialogue. It can improve the design of voice assistants, meeting bots, and other duplex systems that need to handle interruptions gracefully.
visual_elements: A three-way overlap diagram showing continue, adapt, or yield responses
A decision tree for listener intent: backchannel vs collaboration vs interruption
A side-by-side comparison of binary evaluation versus Duplex Cue evaluation
A conversation timeline highlighting overlapping speech and in-turn adaptation moments
paper_title: Continue, Adapt, or Yield: In-Turn Adaptation to Overlapping Speech in Full-Duplex Agents
paper_authors: Yunqi Lu, Tyler Baumgartner, Nikhil Johri, Brandon Tai, Candice Fan
